prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map outlines a cluttered garage/utility space where the camera wearer turns and walks toward a side doorway across the five frames. In Frame 1, a dark hanging coat or draped cloth on the left is brightest and within arm's reach (~0.3–0.6 m), partially occluding a sink counter with potted plants (~2.5–3 m back) that sits about 1–1.5 m left of a closed door and a refrigerator (~2–2.5 m away on the right), with a scooter handle and table edge lower down at ~1 m. Across Frames 2 to 4, as the camera wearer turns left and advances along the corridor toward the back garage door (~5–7 m ahead), the right-hand wall, doorway frame, and shelving move into arm's reach (~0.5–1.2 m) while a person in dark clothing walks ahead (~2.5–3.5 m away, ~1–1.5 m right of the central clutter) facing away and right toward the doorway and never looking at the camera wearer; by Frame 5, the open white interior door and right doorframe fill the foreground within arm's reach (~0.4–0.8 m), occluding the room beyond except for a dark gap at ~2–3 m. Compared to the motion-blurred RGB frames, the depth map clearly separates the foreground wall plane, doorway recess, and central clutter piles from the deep background corridor. However, it is unreliable in Frame 2 where severe motion blur flattens the walking person and floor into an indistinct mid-grey wash, and in Frame 4 where the person entering the recessed doorway blends almost seamlessly into the surrounding doorframe depth.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map detects only a sparse subset of objects across the garage scene, leaving Frames 2 and 4 completely blank. In Frame 1, it labels the dark hanging garment on the far left as a "person" (~0.3–0.6 m away, within the camera wearer's arm's reach and cropped at the left and bottom edges), two "potted plant" instances on the counter (~2.5–3 m ahead, slightly above waist level and ~1.5 m left of the fridge), and the "refrigerator" on the right (~2–2.5 m away, partially occluded at the lower right by a foreground table). In Frame 3, it isolates the actual "person" (~3 m ahead and slightly right of center) facing away and to the right with their right arm within reach of the doorway (~0.4 m in front of them), while missing all surrounding shelves, plants, and floor clutter. In Frame 5, as the camera wearer approaches the doorway within arm's reach (~0.4–0.8 m), the map mislabels the open white paneled door on the left as a "refrigerator" and splits the dark silhouette in the doorway gap on the right (~1.5–2 m away, ~0.5 m right of the door panel, facing away into the adjoining room) into two partial "person" masks truncated by the right doorframe. While segmentation helps sharpen the boundary of the walking person against cluttered shelving in Frame 3 and locates the small potted plants in Frame 1 that blend into the background in RGB, it is highly unreliable due to false-positive class labels (coat as person, door as refrigerator) and complete detection failures during motion blur in Frames 2 and 4.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is entirely blank across Frames 1, 2, 4, and 5, rendering a single yellow upper-body skeleton only in Frame 3 and no magenta hand skeletons in any frame. In Frame 3, this skeleton locates the walking person in the middle distance (~3 m in front of the camera wearer and slightly right of the central aisle), positioned just left of the side doorway and about 1–1.5 m right of the cluttered table. The arrangement of the head, shoulder, torso, and right-arm keypoints shows the person oriented away from the camera wearer and angled toward the right doorway, looking ahead into the doorway rather than back toward the camera, with their raised right forearm extending within arm's reach (~0.3–0.5 m) of the door handle area while their lower body is unmapped and partially occluded by foreground clutter. This skeletal overlay makes the person's forward-leaning torso tilt, head orientation, and raised right arm posture in Frame 3 much easier to read than in the motion-blurred dark clothing of the RGB image. However, the map is largely unreliable across the sequence because motion blur, dim lighting, and severe occlusion by clutter and doorframes cause it to completely miss the person in Frames 2, 4, and 5 as well as the person's legs and hands in Frame 3.
